summary: Dependabot bump of actions/create-github-app-token in the publisher job of the trusted security gate, from v2.2.2 (fee1f7d) to v3.3.0 (64ab729). Only the pinned commit and its version comment change; the step keeps a full commit SHA, the same inputs (app-id, private-key, permission-statuses: write), the same environment (security-gate-publisher), the same eligibility condition and the status-only use of the token. Verified upstream that 64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 is the commit of tag v3.3.0 and that action.yml at that commit still defines app-id, private-key and permission-statuses and runs on node24. The v3.0.0 breaking changes (proxy only via NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY, self-hosted runner v2.327.1 or later) do not apply: the job runs on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest without a proxy. app-id is deprecated in favour of client-id and only emits a warning. The narrow Dependabot exemption of ADR-0050 does not cover this file because its steps use the '- name:' then 'uses:' layout, which the conservative parser does not recognise; a full review is the intended path for the workflow that holds the gate's private key. No new trust boundary, permission, secret or network destination.

findings.evidence: The publisher step hands the GitHub App private key to a third-party action; a compromised action release could misuse it within the installation's permissions.
findings.resolution: Pre-existing and unchanged in scope: the action stays pinned by full commit SHA (now the verified v3.3.0 commit), the minted token is limited to statuses: write and the job runs only from the default branch in the security-gate-publisher environment.

tests.evidence: Inputs app-id (deprecated, use client-id), private-key (required) and permission-statuses exist; runs using node24.

limitations: The trusted gate runs from the default branch, so the new action version is exercised only after the merge; the first PR afterwards shows whether the publisher still posts skirnir/trusted-security-review.
The action's source between v2.2.2 and v3.3.0 was not audited line by line; review relied on the release notes, the pinned commit and action.yml.
Moving from app-id to client-id needs a new repository variable and is left for a separate change.
